# vendor

Third-party assets kept locally so the app runs without a CDN.

Everything here is generated by `build-vendor.py` — don't hand-edit the outputs.
To change a version, edit the constant in that script and re-run it:

```sh
cd vendor
python3 -m venv .venv
./.venv/bin/pip install fonttools brotli
./.venv/bin/python build-vendor.py
```

`fontTools` is needed for the font subsetting and doesn't belong in a Node
project's dependencies, hence the throwaway venv. `.venv/` and `.build/` are
gitignored, and `build.js` skips dot-entries when copying so they never reach
`dist/`.

`index.html` loads everything by **relative path**, so it resolves the same in
dev, in `dist/`, and under `file://`.

## Files

| File | What | When it loads |
|---|---|---|
| `lib.bundle.js` | xlsx 0.20.3 + lz-string 1.5.0 + jspdf 3.0.3 + jspdf-autotable 5.0.2 + pptxgen 3.12.0 | eager — `LZString` is needed during boot to restore shared links |
| `mermaid.min.js` | mermaid 10.9.1 | lazy, on first mermaid render |
| `Pretendard-Regular.ttf` | Pretendard 1.3.9 static TTF | lazy, PDF export only |
| `fonts.css` + 4 `.woff2` | web fonts, see below | per unicode-range, on demand |
| `LICENSES.txt` | SIL OFL 1.1 for all three font families | — |

The five bundled libraries are concatenated in dependency order (autotable
patches jsPDF, so it must follow it) with `;` between them so a file that ends
without a semicolon can't run into the next one.

### CDN fallback

If a local file is missing — someone copied `index.html` on its own — each
loader falls back to its original CDN URL and logs a `console.warn`; a silent
fallback would defeat the point of vendoring. The inline block after
`lib.bundle.js` tests each of the five globals separately and `document.write`s
only what's missing, which is what preserves the original synchronous order.

Version bumps must update **both** this script and the CDN URLs in `index.html`,
or the fallback will quietly serve a different version than the local copy.

There is no fallback for the fonts — a missing file degrades to the CSS fallback
stack on its own.

## Web fonts

Pretendard is **not** a Google Fonts family. The `@import` this replaced silently
dropped it, so body text had been falling back to the system sans-serif all along;
hosting it here is what makes it apply.

The variable font is cut into two **non-overlapping** pieces:

- `pretendard-common.woff2` (462 KB) — Latin, punctuation, box-drawing, and the
  2,350 KS X 1001 Hangul syllables. Covers effectively all real Korean text.
- `pretendard-rest.woff2` (1.3 MB) — the other 8,822 syllables.

The browser fetches only the piece whose `unicode-range` contains what is
actually rendered, so a normal session never requests `rest`. Ranges are disjoint
on purpose: overlapping them would make the outcome depend on `@font-face`
declaration order, which is not worth betting 1.3 MB on. This costs ~32 KB of
generated range lists in `fonts.css` (a few KB gzipped).

JetBrains Mono and Outfit come from `@fontsource-variable` as single variable
files. Note this is a **coverage change** from the previous Google Fonts split:
latin-ext, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese are no longer covered for these two
families. Fine for this app; adding latin-ext back would be two more files.

## Canvas gotcha

Unlike DOM text, `fillText` does **not** trigger a webfont download. With a split
font that means any character the DOM never rendered would silently draw — and
measure — in the fallback face. The `fillText` wrapper next to the canvas setup
in `index.html` requests those characters and re-renders once they arrive.
Removing it brings the bug back.

One residual: exporting content that was never drawn on screen can still bake
fallback glyphs, because `toDataURL()` runs before that async load lands. The
second export is correct.

## Encoding

Several of these bundles contain non-ASCII bytes and must be read as UTF-8. When
a host does not send `charset=utf-8` on the `.js` response (`file://` never does),
the browser falls back to the document's encoding — `index.html` declares
`<meta charset="UTF-8">`, which covers it. Keep that meta tag.
